# Sluice

> Sluice is a C++20 explicit file-I/O library for Linux regular files: one
> shared `File` contract, direct completed-return execution and explicit
> request-based execution with exactly two shipped backends (ThreadPool and
> io_uring), bounded progress, explicit resource ownership and lifetime rules,
> and no host runtime or general task scheduler in the supported surface.

This file is a navigation index, not a specification; it adds no rules and has
no normative force. What wins when sources disagree:

1. [docs/explicit-io-contract.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/explicit-io-contract.md) —
   sole normative root (revision v2-r1). Do not infer APIs from summaries;
   open the linked contract or header.
2. [docs/roadmap/v2-conformance.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/roadmap/v2-conformance.md) —
   what is implemented and what evidence exists, per requirement group.
3. C++ under [include/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/include)
   and [src/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/src) — what a
   commit actually does; a mismatch with the root is a conformance gap, not a
   contract change.
4. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/AGENTS.md) —
   repository working rules (testing discipline, mechanism justification).

Superseded v1 documents and archived records are history; their statuses do
not transfer (see `## Optional`).

## Specification and authority

- [docs/explicit-io-contract.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/explicit-io-contract.md):
  the v2 root. Key sections: §1 product scope (Linux regular-file data I/O
  only), §2 dictionary (TERM-01), §3 workloads W-01/W-02/W-03, §6 File
  semantics, §7 errors and partial effects, §8–9 request core and handles,
  §10 observation, §11 progress and external-host integration, §12 borrow
  lifetime, §13 threading, §14 cancellation, §15 closed backend seam,
  §17 shutdown and destruction, §18 resource bounds, §19 verification rules,
  §23 decision tables.
- [docs/roadmap/v2-conformance.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/roadmap/v2-conformance.md):
  conformance ledger (groups G1–G10, release gates RG1–RG7). Every `VERIFIED`
  is bounded to a stated property, commit and configuration — a passing test
  or model at one commit is not a universal correctness proof.
- [README.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/README.md):
  product overview with an informative architecture diagram;
  [docs/README.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/README.md)
  maps current authority versus dated evidence;
  [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)
  records release history and the v2 breaking-change disclosure.

## Public SDK: libraries, headers, build and install

Build system is [xmake](https://xmake.io); a C++20 compiler and Linux are
required. `sluice_core` (File + shared semantics + direct execution) has no
async dependency; `sluice_async` (request execution) depends on `sluice_core`
and is opt-in. `--liburing=y` / `--liburing=n` are different build profiles:
`n` ships an honest io_uring stub with no `SLUICE_HAS_LIBURING`; `y` requires
a real liburing. `xmake install -o <prefix> sluice_core sluice_async` installs
the public headers plus `libsluice_core.a` / `libsluice_async.a`; consumers
compile/link against the prefix directly (e.g. `-L<prefix>/lib
-lsluice_core -lsluice_async`; a liburing=y build additionally links
`-luring`). No CMake package config or exported CMake
targets are provided or verified.

The installed public surface is exactly these 11 headers
(`xmake/libraries.lua` allowlist; root Appendix B). Everything else — the
backend classes, the `AsyncBackend` seam and all `detail/` headers — is
internal and uninstalled; do not treat `detail/` paths as SDK.

- [include/sluice/file_resource.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/file_resource.hpp):
  `File` RAII owner, open modes, `FileInfo`/identity, `native_handle()` borrow.
- [include/sluice/blocking/file.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/blocking/file.hpp):
  direct completed-return operations (`read_at`/`write_at`, `read`/`write`,
  `sync_data`/`sync_all`, `file_info`, `size`, `resize`) and short-I/O
  compositions (`read_exact*`, `write_all*`).
- [include/sluice/result.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/result.hpp),
  [error.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/error.hpp),
  [effect.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/effect.hpp),
  [measurement.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/measurement.hpp):
  `Result<T>`/`IoError` vocabulary, confirmed-bytes-vs-unknown effect
  reporting, non-authoritative diagnostics.
- [include/sluice/async/async_io_context.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/async_io_context.hpp):
  `AsyncIoContext` (six `submit_*` ops, `cancel`, `lookup`, `poll_progress`,
  `wait_one`, `claim_progress_owner`, `progress_notification_fd()`,
  `acknowledge_progress_notification()`, `detach_progress_host()`,
  `close_admission`/`request_stop`/`shutdown`, observer attach/cancel,
  `delivery_retired`), `ProgressPass` (including `dispatch_retry_remains`),
  `ProgressOwner`.
- [include/sluice/async/request.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/request.hpp):
  move-only `Request<T>` (`ready`, `try_result`, `take_result`, `discard`,
  `cancel`), `RequestId`, `CancelDisposition`, `RequestReadiness`.
- [include/sluice/async/request_scope.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/request_scope.hpp):
  `RequestScope` + `ScopeTicket<T>` bounded owned-driver pipeline scope.
- [include/sluice/async/threadpool_backend.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/threadpool_backend.hpp)
  and [uring_backend.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/uring_backend.hpp):
  the only context factories — `make_threadpool_context(ThreadPoolConfig)`
  (throws on setup failure) and `make_uring_context(UringConfig)` returning
  `Result` with an explicit `not_supported` when the build has no io_uring
  profile. Neither falls back to another execution.
- [xmake.lua](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/xmake.lua) +
  [xmake/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/xmake): targets,
  sanitizer modes, the liburing switch (`xmake/uring.lua`) and the installed
  header allowlist (`xmake/libraries.lua`).
- [scripts/verify_v2_package.py](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/scripts/verify_v2_package.py):
  independent verification entry — installs into a fresh prefix, gates the
  11-header surface, compiles/links/runs clean-room consumers against the
  installed prefix only, in both liburing profiles. Its recorded scope is the
  dated manifests under
  [docs/evidence/v2-release-acceptance-20261017/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/docs/evidence/v2-release-acceptance-20261017).
- [tests/package/consumers/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/tests/package/consumers):
  clean-room external-consumer examples compiled against the installed
  prefix only — `w01_direct.cpp`, `w02_pipeline.cpp`, `w03_external_loop.cpp`
  and per-contract micro-consumers are the most faithful usage examples.
- [apps/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/apps): four reference
  applications (sluice-copy/hash/grep/tail) built on the public surface.

## Execution models

- W-01 Ordinary utility (direct): open, read/write at explicit or shared
  cursor, sync, metadata — completed-return calls on the caller thread with no
  context, worker or request table. Authority: root §3 W-01, §6–7; public API
  [blocking/file.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/blocking/file.hpp).
- W-02 Bounded pipeline (`RequestScope`): submit up to a chosen bound, tolerate
  short I/O and admission rejection, settle every accepted request on normal,
  early and exceptional exit. Authority: root §3 W-02, §16; public API
  [request_scope.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/request_scope.hpp).
- W-03 External event loop: the application owns its loop and the single
  fixed progress owner; it integrates the pollable notification fd, submits
  and reaps bounded work, and shuts down without busy polling. Authority:
  root §3 W-03, §11 (PROG-01..04), §13 (THREAD-01), §17; public API
  [async_io_context.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/async_io_context.hpp)
  (`poll_progress`, `wait_one`, `progress_notification_fd()`,
  `acknowledge_progress_notification()`, `detach_progress_host()`).

Note: "Direct" names Sluice's direct completed-return invocation model
(W-01). It is not the Linux `O_DIRECT` open flag; Sluice never sets
`O_DIRECT`, and the two concepts are unrelated.

## Async request lifecycle and progress — read before writing an adapter

The authoritative protocol is the root, not any summary: §5 (INV: initiation
never waits), §8 (REQ: acceptance, publication, reclaim), §9 (HANDLE:
`Request<T>` states and destruction), §10 (OBS: observer attach/deliver/
retire), §11 (PROG: driver contract, no-lost-wake, external loop), §12
(LIFE: borrows), §14 (CANCEL), §17 (SHUT). C++ entry points live in
[async_io_context.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/async_io_context.hpp)
and
[request.hpp](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/include/sluice/async/request.hpp).

Cautions that follow directly from the root (each link above defines the
exact conditions; the summaries do not replace them):

- A returned `Request` means acceptance, not completion; submission never
  waits for I/O or capacity (INV-02). Acceptance, publication, observation
  and consumption are distinct events (REQ-03..05, HANDLE-01).
- A notification is a progress-availability signal, not a completion
  guarantee and never a drain authority (PROG-01, PROG-03, TERM-01).
  `ExecutionClosed` shutdown retains unconsumed results (SHUT-01);
  notification does not mean every published result has been consumed.
- Reuse of buffers or the `File` follows an acquired public terminal —
  observing it via `ready()`/`try_result()`/`take_result()`/`lookup()`.
  Physical completion alone, a cancel disposition, a wait timeout or observer
  cancellation never ends the borrow (REQ-04, LIFE-01, CANCEL-02).
- Cancel is best-effort: `requested` and
  `physical_interruption_unsupported` do not mean the I/O stopped, and a
  cancel completion does not prove the operation's buffer is unreachable
  (CANCEL-01/02, BACKEND-03).
- `poll_progress()`/`wait_one()`/driving `shutdown()` belong to the single
  fixed progress owner (PROG-01, THREAD-01). Do not park host ASYNC worker
  threads inside `wait_one()` to emulate completion-driven execution; host
  workers integrate via the notification fd and the owner drives.
- A `ProgressPass` with `dispatch_retry_remains` set owes another bounded
  pass: that accepted transport has not reached the kernel, produces no
  completion and no notification until submitted, so an fd-only wait strands
  it (PROG-01). A temporarily unreadable notification fd is not evidence that
  dispatch/progress work is finished (PROG-03).
- Shutdown: any thread may call `close_admission()`/`request_stop()`;
  driving `shutdown()` and context destruction require the owner and zero
  live public bindings (SHUT-01..04, HANDLE-03).

## Correctness evidence: tests, formal models, package verification

- [tests/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/tests): deterministic
  suites run as xmake targets (`xmake run <target>`). Landmarks:
  `semantic_*` (File-semantics oracle suites), `backend_contract_conformance_{threadpool,uring}_test`
  (cross-backend contract conformance), `public_request_test`,
  `request_core_protocol_test`, `request_scope_test`,
  `threadpool_progress_pass_bound_test`, `threadpool_external_loop_test`,
  `uring_progress_race_test`, `uring_owed_residue_test`,
  `uring_external_loop_test`, `shutdown_lifecycle_test` (plus its `_uring`
  variant), `request_error_domain_{threadpool,uring}_test`. Target
  definitions:
  [xmake/tests.lua](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/xmake/tests.lua).
- [formal/tla/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/formal/tla): four
  living bounded TLA+ models mirroring C++ transitions — `RequestCore`,
  `ObserverCore`, `ProgressSource`, `ShutdownCore`. Gates:
  [scripts/verify_tla.sh](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/scripts/verify_tla.sh)
  and
  [scripts/verify_progress_source_model.sh](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/scripts/verify_progress_source_model.sh).
  Scope and non-coverage: root VERIFY-06; evidence state: ledger G8. A model
  PASS proves only its explored instances under stated fairness assumptions.
- [scripts/verify_v2_package.py](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/scripts/verify_v2_package.py)
  (+ [tests/package/README.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/tests/package/README.md)):
  the external-consumer package-boundary verification described above.
- [docs/evidence/v2-release-acceptance-20261017/verification-record.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/evidence/v2-release-acceptance-20261017/verification-record.md):
  release-acceptance record — 8-cell build matrix (per-cell compiler/mode/
  liburing; kernel and filesystem recorded once in the same directory's
  `environment.txt`); per-cell argv/exit logs in
  [matrix/matrix.json](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/evidence/v2-release-acceptance-20261017/matrix/matrix.json).
  Configurations outside the recorded matrix are untested by that release.

## Performance research

- [docs/performance/methodology.md](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/docs/performance/methodology.md):
  standing method — freeze (commit SHA, host, compiler/flags, workload,
  correctness oracle, measurement config) before the first run; baseline
  before profiling; single-factor attribution; paired A/B on one host.
- [bench/](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/tree/master/bench): harness for
  the preregistered G0 matrix ([run_matrix.sh](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/bench/run_matrix.sh),
  [check_run.py](https://github.com/jnhu76/Sluice/blob/master/bench/check_run.py));
  a new workload needs its own runner configuration before results count as
  evidence.

For external integrations (e.g. a DuckDB or fio adapter), the method applies
to the composed system: verify semantics and the actual I/O path first
(which Sluice backend really executed, how many bytes/requests Sluice
actually served), distinguish Direct/ThreadPool/io_uring by their real
execution semantics, and never attribute adapter overhead to Sluice (or
conversely) without measurement. Label results with source commit, build
profile, backend, cache state and measurement configuration. Adapter
experiments are external workloads: no adapter ships here, and this
repository does not bind any consumer version or benchmark parameters.
